speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You are late for a candle that was lit at five. The hall candle is the firing sixpence, and the washing is in the same sixpence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not going to read. Broth, if it is ready. The jaw is still tender. I am not calling it quiet.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Look at the hem of your cloak. You have brought the mud of Shoreditch in on the wool.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it until it is dry. If you brush it wet, you will streak it from the hem to the knee.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Leave it, Alse. The mud can wait on a dry morning. The broth cannot.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: She lit the candle while you were out. Gib sat under it until I moved him off the flame.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him any place that is not the flame. I brought nothing home to read, and I want nothing put in front of me.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: There is a book on the shelf, if this is only pride.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is not pride. I am reading nothing. Not the lovers, not a letter, not a page for the sake of having read.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I will not carry a candle upstairs unless you ask. The hall has the one she lit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The hall is enough until church. After church I am for bed, and the cat may have my feet.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Evening prayer, and then bed. The sun was down before five. That is why the candle is already old.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I was in a passage while she lit it. The share is thirty-six shillings. I have not spent them.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will not ask where thirty-six shillings sit. I only know the word, and the mud.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Nor will I. Sit the money where you sit money. Do not make my supper an accounting.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will write the line when I have eaten, and I will not write a total under it. The broth first.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The broth is the threepence, as on Sunday. Soft. There is no crust on your side.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No crust. And no new telling of the dead man. He is dead. I asked who pays. I was not told the manner of his end.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The hem will still be muddy in the morning, if I leave it as you said.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it will still be muddy. I would rather a dry brush on Monday than a wet streak tonight.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eat. I am not walking you to church. You know the hour as well as I do.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can walk as far as St Helen's. I am not walking further, and I am not taking a book.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: He will want the bed when you are back. He has his own ideas about feet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He may have the feet. I mean to be in before the Bow bell, if the prayer stays a prayer.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mark me. Broth, the sixpence already burned in that candle, nothing read, and bed when the church has done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is the bill. Thirty-six shillings stay in the house. I have no purchase in me tonight.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. Eat the broth before it cools. The hem stays on the peg until it is dry.
